title: Beyond Accuracy: A Qualitative Analysis of Vision-Language Models for Hate Speech Detection in Memes
abstract: arXiv:2608.26143v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Memes have turned out to be a powerful tool through which individuals share their ideas concerning contemporary social and political problems. Their anonymity, as well as their ability to go viral, make them a powerful medium for spreading hate. It remains very difficult to identify such complex and context-dependent hate speech. Although they display excellent performance on multimodal tasks, vision-language models (VLMs) tend to ignore context, irony, and other subtle cues that play a key role in identifying hateful memes. In this work, we present a qualitative analysis of four state-of-the-art VLMs: LLaVA-7B, Qwen-VL, GPT-4o mini, and Claude 3 Haiku. We evaluate these models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting to examine how contextual framing influences their outputs. translated_title: 超越准确性：视觉语言模型在梗图仇恨言论检测中的定性分析
translated_abstract: 梗图已成为个人分享对当代社会和政治问题看法的一种强大工具。其匿名性及快速传播的能力，使其成为传播仇恨的有力媒介。识别这种复杂且依赖上下文的仇恨言论仍然非常困难。尽管视觉语言模型（VLMs）在多模态任务上表现出色，但它们往往忽视上下文、讽刺及其他在识别仇恨梗图中起关键作用的微妙线索。在本研究中，我们对四种最先进的视觉语言模型进行了定性分析：LLaVA-7B、Qwen-VL、GPT-4o mini和Claude 3 Haiku。我们在零样本和少样本提示条件下评估这些模型，以检验上下文框架如何影响其输出。我们的分析超越了简单的分类准确性，侧重于对模型生成的理由进行定性评估，从而提供更深入的见解。
tldr: 本研究通过定性分析四种视觉语言模型在梗图仇恨言论检测中的表现，揭示了它们在理解上下文和讽刺方面的局限性，并强调了超越分类准确性的评估重要性。
en_tdlr: This study provides a qualitative analysis of four vision-language models for hate speech detection in memes, revealing their limitations in understanding context and irony, and emphasizing the importance of evaluating beyond classification accuracy.
